header:
Date: 2026-08-21 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 56m
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Maya (Mariner Sec), Ethan (Mariner Infra), Samir (Mariner DevOps)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Mariner Health through SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning patterns, a proposed least-privilege RBAC model for product and admin roles, and encryption/KMS integration options (BYOK, HSM). Customers requested SOC2/ISO artifacts, SCIM mapping template and a short POC to validate provisioning and audit log exports to Splunk. Several clarifications about EU data residency and audit retention windows were discussed.
topics: SAML SSO setup and assertion attributes
RBAC role definitions and least privilege
Audit logs, export formats and SIEM integration
Encryption: KMS BYOK and HSM options
questions: Can Redwood accept signed SAML assertions with ADFS?
How granular can SCIM provisioning be (group vs user-level)?
What audit log retention windows are available and can logs be pushed to Splunk/Datadog?
Does Redwood Private support HSM/BYOK for model keys and who rotates keys?
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Welcome everyone, thanks for carving out time. Today Jonah and I will run through our recommended SAML/SCIM handoff and a least-privilege RBAC model. Maya, Ethan, Samir — thanks for joining.
[00:12] Maya: Yeah thanks. We wanted to use this to validate we can onboard quickly; main constraints are SOC 2 needs, EU data residency for some workloads, and very strict least-privilege.
[00:22] Jonah: Got it. Quick agenda: SSO auth flow, SCIM group sync, role mappings, audit logs and KMS. We'll flag the parts that differ between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:34] Ethan: Can you remind us which differences are material for SAML? Like do you need any special connectors for Private?
[00:40] Jonah: For Private you host the control plane in your VPC, so the SAML redirect endpoints are internal to your network if you choose. For Hosted we do standard SAML 2.0 SP endpoints; nothing special for the IdP side. Occasionally we see attribute names different — that's the main friction.
[00:55] Samir: Attribute names — yeah, our IdP is Okta but we also have an internal AD FS instance for legacy apps; assertion formats sometimes differ.
[01:04] Jonah: Ok, that's common. We recommend mapping on email/username + a groups claim. For AD FS we can accept the urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress variant — we've seen transcribers read that as name id email but it works.
[01:20] Maya: Two quick things: one, we need SCIM to provision groups so we can enforce joiner/leaver flows. Two, we want at least two granular admin roles — org-admin and audit-reader — with separation of duties.
[01:31] Aisha: That makes sense. Jonah, can you sketch a simple role matrix?
[01:35] Jonah: Sure. Proposal: Managed roles: 'svc-app' (service account for applications, no UI), 'user' (default limited generation access), 'editor' (can create prompts/pipelines), 'admin' (can deploy model rollouts), 'sec-audit' (read-only audit logs and exports). We map SCIM groups to those roles. For least-privilege you should keep admin count small and use an audit-reader role for compliance teams.
[01:58] Ethan: Do we get token-level metadata in the audit logs, like which model variant and the route, for traceability? We need to map back to our SIEM.
[02:08] Jonah: Yes, our audit payload includes token usage, model id, model version, route name, and requester identity from the SAML/SCIM mapping. It can be delivered as syslog or forwarded via an HTTP push. Sample schema we'll share. Note: some fields can appear mangled in transcripts like 'K V cache' — that's the KV cache we report metrics for.
[02:28] Maya: Retention — what are retention defaults? We need at least 12 months of granular logs for SOC 2 audit trails.
[02:36] Aisha: Hosted tiers default to 90 days for high-detail logs, longer retention is an add-on. Dedicated and Private deployments can extend retention per contract. For Mariner we can include 12 months in the Dedicated proposal.
[02:52] Samir: For SCIM, can we sync nested groups? Our team structure is nested with department -> subteam. We don't want to manage too many mappings.
[03:02] Jonah: SCIM v2 supports group membership lists, but nested groups are not standardized across IdPs. We typically recommend syncing top-level groups and using an attribute for 'department' to refine role assignments. We'll give you a mapping template — e.g., scim.groups -> role, scim.userName -> principal.
[03:20] Ethan: About KMS — can we bring our own key (BYOK)? We must have keys under our control for certain PHI-affiliated workloads.
[03:28] Jonah: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM — we integrate with AWS KMS and can support Cloud HSM setups. For Hosted we support BYOK via a key proxy and rotation policy; key material never leaves HSM. We'll send the crypto architecture doc.
[03:44] Maya: Who is responsible for rotating the keys and how is that logged?
[03:48] Jonah: Rotation is customer-driven for BYOK. We surface rotation events in audit logs (key id, rotation timestamp, operator principal). For our managed keys we rotate per our internal policy and publish rotation events as well.
[04:01] Maya: Good. I heard earlier mention of HSM, the customers sometimes call that an H S M, right?
[04:06] Jonah: (laughs) yes, HSM — hardware security module.
[04:09] Aisha: Let's talk SCIM provisioning flows. Jonah, demo the two common flows: just-in-time SAML provisioning vs full SCIM push.
[04:18] Jonah: Right. Just-in-time (JIT) provisioning creates users on first login — light touch, no group sync. SCIM push actively creates and updates users and groups. For least-privilege we recommend SCIM so you can map groups to roles and revoke access centrally.
[04:35] Ethan: And for service accounts? We want programmatic service identities that don't rely on user's SCIM accounts. How do we do that?
[04:42] Jonah: We support service accounts with key pairs and scoped roles. You can create a 'svc-app' role and issue a short-lived token bound to it. Rotate the keys regularly; we support automatic rotation and audit entries.
[04:55] Samir: Are service account tokens present in the same audit stream or separated? We want to distinguish human from machine.
[05:01] Jonah: They are tagged in the logs as service principals. You can filter them in your SIEM.
[05:06] Maya: About RBAC policy enforcement — can we require MFA for admin role elevation?
[05:11] Jonah: We don't enforce MFA directly — that's handled by your IdP. We can honor an attribute in SAML assertion that indicates MFA. You can add a precondition that admin role only binds when assertion includes 'amr' or similar MFA claim.
[05:24] Ethan: Nice. How about attribute mapping specifics — what field do you need for email vs username?
[05:29] Jonah: Prefer email as name identifier. If you use uid we accept it but we need a stable immutable id. We'll provide an example SAML assertion with attribute names.
[05:38] Maya: For SCIM we want to auto-add new employees to 'user' and the oncall team to 'editor' automatically. Is that straightforward?
[05:45] Jonah: Yes, via group-to-role mapping. We'll show you the JSON example — SCIM group 'oncall' maps to 'editor' role. There's also an 'entitlements' attribute for finer control.
[05:55] Samir: Entitlements — does Redwood support custom entitlements or feature flags per role?
[05:59] Jonah: We support custom entitlements per role. They are attached to role metadata and enforced at runtime. We'll include examples.
[06:08] Aisha: Shifting to audit exports — what's the latency and throughput for log export? We need to ensure we don't drop events during spikes.
[06:17] Jonah: We publish events reliably to our internal pipeline and can forward them via a durable queue to your SIEM. Latency is typically under 30s for standard logs, under 10s for critical audit events. We guarantee delivery retries for transient failures. For very high throughput we recommend Dedicated lanes with a higher SLA.
[06:36] Ethan: Do you support common SIEM connectors or do we need to set up a pull?
[06:41] Jonah: We support pushing to syslog (RFC5424), an HTTP webhook with batching, and a Splunk HEC endpoint. We'll include a sample configuration for Splunk.
[06:51] Maya: On data residency — we have EU customers where data must stay in the EU. If we use Hosted, can we pin workloads to eu-west (Ireland)?
[06:59] Aisha: Yes, we have region pinning. For Hosted we can provision model endpoints in eu-west-1 and store audit logs in EU regions, but that requires contract-level commitments for residency and sometimes Dedicated or Private is recommended for stricter controls.
[07:15] Ethan: For PII-heavy requests we might want Private deployment. Would the RBAC model be the same?
[07:21] Jonah: The model is identical; config surfaces differ. Private gives you ultimate control over networking and KMS. The policy model and SCIM mapping are the same YAML/JSON we use for Hosted. You can export/import the mapping.
[07:34] Samir: Any gotchas integrating AD FS? We had odd behavior with groupName vs displayName mismatches before.
[07:40] Jonah: AD FS often uses sAMAccountName vs displayName. We'll accept both but need a mapping. Also AD FS sometimes sends group SIDs instead of names; we can map SIDs if you provide a translation table.
[07:55] Maya: Can we get visibility on who changed role bindings? For SOC 2 we need an immutable change log.
[08:01] Jonah: Yes, role binding changes are audit events with initiator identity, timestamp, and previous/new state. They are tamper-evident in our audit pipeline and can be exported to your SIEM.
[08:12] Ethan: About log format — is it JSON lines?
[08:15] Jonah: JSONL is the default. We'll include schema v1 in the artifacts.
[08:20] Maya: Are there specific fields for request/response redaction? We have to ensure PHI isn't retained in logs.
[08:27] Jonah: We support configurable redaction rules at ingestion; by default we redact a small set of PII-like patterns. For PHI-sensitive workloads you can enable stronger redaction or route those requests to Private so logs are controlled by your policies.
[08:42] Samir: How about retention windows for alerts and high fidelity logs? Can we tier storage?
[08:47] Jonah: Yes, we support hot (90 days), warm (365 days), and cold (multi-year) tiers for audit artifacts. Hot tier keeps full granularity, warm is compressed, and cold is aggregated. We'll indicate tradeoffs.
[09:00] Aisha: Quick question from sales perspective — what's the typical timeline to go from SAML test to full SCIM sync in a POC?
[09:07] Jonah: Usually 1-2 weeks. SAML testing can take a day if SSO metadata is available. SCIM mapping and group sync plus role validation — 3-7 business days. If AD FS quirks appear, it can extend.
[09:20] Ethan: Can we do an automated smoke test that validates a sample user's access matrix after provisioning?
[09:25] Jonah: Yes, our onboarding harness can run a smoke test to assert group membership -> role mapping -> effective permissions. We'll run that as part of the POC.
[09:34] Maya: On legal/compliance — do you provide a data processing agreement and subprocessors list?
[09:39] Aisha: Yes, DPA and subprocessor list are provided during procurement; I'll attach them.
[09:44] Samir: For encryption at rest — you said AWS KMS. Do you also support envelope encryption for model artifacts?
[09:51] Jonah: We use envelope encryption — model artifacts are encrypted with a data key which is encrypted by your KMS key. That helps with key rotation.
[09:58] Maya: Any nuances for Dedicated vs Hosted for envelope encryption?
[10:01] Jonah: Dedicated gives you an option to bring your KMS in the same VPC, reducing egress of key requests. Hosted uses a secure proxy to reach customer KMS for BYOK.
[10:12] Ethan: How do you record access to the keys themselves — is there a key access audit?
[10:15] Jonah: KMS access logs are available (CloudTrail or equivalent). We surface key usage events in our audit stream as well.
[10:22] Maya: We have an external auditor in September — would you be able to provide sample logs and attestations for a short review?
[10:28] Aisha: Absolutely, we'll provide a SOC 2 bridge letter and sample logs scoped to the POC.
[10:34] Samir: One more on SCIM: can we do attribute transformations? For example, IdP gives department as 'HR-US' and we want 'HR' in the role map.
[10:42] Jonah: We support simple regex-based transformations and attribute mapping rules. We'll include examples.
[10:49] Ethan: About SAML signing algorithms — we use SHA-256 only, some older apps still send SHA-1.
[10:55] Jonah: We require SHA-256 for production; we can accept SHA-1 in test for legacy reasons but recommend updating.
[11:04] Maya: Does Redwood support Just-in-time group provisioning with custom provisioning hooks?
[11:09] Jonah: We have hooks that can call out to a customer webhook during provisioning. That can be used to enrich user objects.
[11:16] Aisha: Great. let's surface the key deliverables and owners. Jonah, can you summarise the artifacts you'll share?
[11:22] Jonah: I'll share: SCIM mapping template (JSON), SAML assertion example, audit schema JSONL file, Splunk HEC config sample, and the KMS/BYOK architecture note.
[11:31] Aisha: And I'll share SOC 2 Type II, ISO attestation, DPA and subprocessor list.
[11:36] Maya: We'll provide IdP metadata and a list of groups we want to sync plus the EU residency confirmation.
[11:41] Samir: Also we'll try to spin up a staging Okta app and invite Jonah into the tester org.
[11:46] Aisha: Perfect. Any final concerns or blockers?
[11:49] Maya: One ask — can we get a quick runbook for emergency access revocation? In case a credential is compromised.
[11:56] Jonah: Yes, emergency revoke runbook is part of the onboarding docs; it includes steps to disable SCIM sync and rotate service keys plus revoke sessions.
[12:07] Ethan: And for the POC, can we keep audit log retention at 12 months to exercise the retention lifecycle?
[12:13] Aisha: We'll propose that in the Dedicated POC terms.
[12:18] Maya: Okay that's it from me, thanks folks.
[12:21] Aisha: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite for the POC week.
[12:27] Jonah: Thanks, bye.
[12:30] [call end]

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-hearings — 'KV cache' heard as 'K V cache'; 'HSM' sometimes spelled out as 'H S M' in notes; minor punctuation/word swap artifacts typical of automated transcription.
